questions.question_text: Which practice is explicitly prohibited in Wyoming real estate transactions?
questions.explanation: Wyoming expressly bans dual agency: W.S. 33-28-302(o) states that 'a licensee shall not establish dual agency with any seller or buyer,' and 33-28-302(k) allows a licensee to be an agent for the seller or for the buyer 'but not as an agent for both.' Exclusive buyer agency (33-28-304) and seller-only agency (33-28-303) are both permitted, and Wyoming's version of transaction brokerage — the non-agency 'intermediary' relationship of 33-28-305 — is the lawful way for one licensee, or two designated licensees in the same company, to assist both sides. Only dual agency itself is prohibited.

questions.question_text: A broker deposits a client's earnest money into the broker's personal checking account. What violation has occurred?
questions.explanation: Depositing client funds into a personal account constitutes commingling, which is a serious violation of Wyoming real estate law. Client funds must be deposited into a properly maintained trust or escrow account, kept separate from the broker's personal or business operating funds.

questions.question_text: A licensee tells a buyer that a property has no foundation issues, knowing the seller disclosed cracks. What violation is this?
questions.explanation: Knowingly making false statements about a material property condition constitutes fraud and misrepresentation, a ground for discipline under Wyoming law. The licensee had actual knowledge of the foundation issues from the seller's disclosure and deliberately concealed this information from the buyer.

questions.question_text: A licensee is convicted of felony embezzlement. How does this affect their Wyoming real estate license?
questions.correct_answer: It is grounds for WREC discipline
distractors: No effect unless real estate related
The license is unaffected until sentencing
questions.explanation: W.S. 33-28-111(a)(xxii) makes discipline available for 'conviction of a felony that relates to the practice of real estate activity or to the ability to perform the duties of a licensee or any felony sexual offense or violent crime.' Embezzlement is squarely within that ground because it goes to the licensee's ability to handle other people's money — a core licensee duty — even though the crime itself was not a real estate transaction. Note the limit: Wyoming does not make every felony an automatic ground, and the statute contains no 'moral turpitude' language; a wholly unrelated non-violent felony would have to be reached through the Commission's catch-all rule against violating state or federal law (018-6 Wyo. Code R. § 6-1(a)(iv)). WREC may fine, censure, place on probation, suspend or revoke.

questions.question_text: A Wyoming salesperson repeatedly fails to give the parties completed copies of signed documents and, when WREC investigates a complaint, cannot produce the transaction file. Which ground for discipline applies?
questions.correct_answer: Failing to deliver documents and to produce records under investigation
questions.explanation: Wyoming's grounds for discipline are a specific, conduct-by-conduct list in W.S. 33-28-111(a). Two items are hit here: (a)(xxi), 'failing to deliver within a reasonable time a completed copy of any document to all parties,' and (a)(xii), 'unreasonably failing to produce documents of record in his possession or under his control concerning any real estate transaction under investigation by the commission.' WREC rule 018-6 § 6-1(a)(x) adds failing to provide information requested relative to a complaint, investigation, or audit. Note that Wyoming — unlike many states — has NO general 'incompetence or negligence' ground; sloppy practice is charged under the specific paragraph it violates.

questions.question_text: Who may file a complaint against a Wyoming real estate licensee with WREC?
questions.correct_answer: Any person may file a complaint
distractors: Only consumers involved in a transaction
Only other licensed real estate agents
questions.explanation: WREC Rules Chapter 8, Section 2(a) provides that a complaint 'may be submitted by any person or entity, a Commission member, or a member of the Commission staff' — the complainant need not be a party to the transaction or a licensee. The complaint must be a sworn written complaint bearing the complainant's notarized signature; WREC cannot accept anonymous or unsigned complaints. Separately, W.S. 33-28-111(a) lets the Commission investigate 'upon its own motion' even with no complaint on file.

questions.question_text: During a disciplinary proceeding, where are formal hearings held?
questions.explanation: Disciplinary matters are set for a formal contested case hearing before the Commission (WREC Rules ch. 8, § 4(c)(ii)), conducted under the Wyoming Administrative Procedure Act and the Office of Administrative Hearings' uniform contested-case rules. W.S. 33-28-113(a) also permits the Commission to contract with an independent hearing officer — who may not be a commission member or employee — to take the evidence and forward written findings of fact and conclusions of law to the Commission, which issues the final order. District court is not where the hearing happens; it is where judicial review is sought afterward, in the county where the violation allegedly occurred (W.S. 33-28-113(c)).

questions.question_text: WREC receives a complaint and begins an investigation. During the process, can WREC examine the broker's records?
questions.correct_answer: Yes — the licensee must produce the records on WREC's request
distractors: Only with the broker's written permission
Only after obtaining a court subpoena
Only if the complaint involves trust funds
questions.explanation: Access to records is a condition of licensure, not something WREC must litigate for. W.S. 33-28-122(a)(iii) requires every responsible broker to 'permit the commission or its representative to examine the responsible broker's trust accounting records,' and WREC Rules ch. 5 § 2 lets the Commission audit those accounts. In an investigation, W.S. 33-28-111(a)(xii) makes it a disciplinable offense to unreasonably fail 'to produce documents of record... concerning any real estate transaction under investigation by the commission,' and rule 018-6 § 6-1(a)(x) covers failing to provide information requested relative to a complaint, investigation, or audit. No broker consent and no court order is required, and the authority is not limited to trust-fund complaints. (Formal subpoenas are a separate tool, available under the Administrative Procedure Act once a contested case is pending — W.S. 16-3-107(c), 16-3-112(b)(ii).)

questions.question_text: After a hearing, WREC finds a licensee guilty of commingling. Which combination of sanctions can WREC impose?
distractors: Only one sanction may be imposed per case
questions.explanation: WREC Rule 018-6 § 6-1 expressly authorizes 'an administrative fine, censure, probation, suspension, or revocation, including a combination thereof.' W.S. 33-28-111(a) lets the Commission impose an administrative fine of up to $2,500 for each separate offense and censure, place on probation, suspend or revoke — so suspension plus a fine for commingling (a ground under 33-28-111(a)(xiv)) is a routine outcome. Fines are credited to the public school fund of the county where the violation occurred (33-28-111(c)). Additional education is typically imposed through a settlement the Commission accepts rather than as a stand-alone sanction. WREC cannot impose jail or criminal fines; criminal penalties for unlicensed activity are prosecuted in court under W.S. 33-28-114.

questions.question_text: WREC identifies a pattern of consumer complaints about a brokerage but no individual has filed a formal complaint. Can WREC act?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, WREC can self-initiate an investigation
distractors: No, a formal complaint is always required
No, WREC must wait for the Attorney General
Yes, but only if 10 or more complaints exist
questions.explanation: W.S. 33-28-111(a) authorizes the Commission to investigate a licensee 'upon a written sworn complaint or... upon its own motion' — no consumer complaint is required. In practice a Commission member or staff member may file the sworn written complaint that opens the file (WREC Rules ch. 8 § 2(a)), after which the matter goes to the Commission investigator and a Liaison Commission Member. There is no minimum number of complaints and no need to wait for the Attorney General, although the AG's office prosecutes the contested case (W.S. 33-28-120).
